claim: Kais Saied won the October 13, 2019 presidential election with 72.71% of the vote (2.77M ballots) vs Nabil Karoui (27.29%).
qualification: Official ISIE definitive results published in JORT n° 85 (2019).

claim: On July 25, 2021, President Kais Saied invoked Article 80 of the 2014 Constitution, suspended parliament (ARP), and dismissed Prime Minister Hichem Mechichi.
qualification: Presidential Decrees 2021-80 and 2021-81 in JORT n° 64 (2021).

claim: Presidential Decree 117 of September 22, 2021 concentrated legislative and executive powers in the presidency and suspended conflicting chapters of the 2014 Constitution.
qualification: Published in JORT n° 86 (2021).

claim: The High Judicial Council (CSM) was dissolved via Decree-Law 2022-11 and replaced by a provisional council.
qualification: Promulgated in JORT n° 16 (Feb 12, 2022).

claim: Presidential Decree 2022-516 revoked 57 magistrates on June 1, 2022; the Administrative Court issued a suspension order for 49 on August 9, 2022.
qualification: Decree in JORT n° 60 (2022); Administrative Court injunction unexecuted by Ministry of Justice.

claim: The 2022 Constitution was approved on July 25, 2022 with 94.6% yes votes on 30.5% turnout.
qualification: Promulgated in JORT n° 89 (August 17, 2022).

claim: Decree-Law 2022-54 Article 24 penalizes publishing false news or rumors with up to 5 years imprisonment (10 years if public officials targeted).
qualification: Promulgated in JORT n° 103 (September 13, 2022).

claim: Kais Saied was re-elected on October 6, 2024 with 90.69% of the vote on 28.8% turnout.
qualification: Official ISIE definitive results bulletin published October 11, 2024.

claim: Real GDP growth was +1.5% in 2019 vs +0.8% in Q2 2026 (YoY).
qualification: 2019 is annual full-year result; 2026 is preliminary quarterly year-on-year annualized observation.

claim: Overall unemployment rate was 14.9% in 2019 vs 16.0% in Q2 2026.
qualification: INS Labour Force Survey (Enquête Nationale sur l'Emploi).

claim: Higher education graduate unemployment was 28.0% in 2019 vs 38.8% in 2026.
qualification: INS Quarterly Employment Survey, higher education degree holders.

claim: Headline consumer inflation was 6.7% in 2019 vs 7.0% in Summer 2026 (Food inflation: 9.8%).
qualification: INS Consumer Price Index (IPC) monthly bulletins.

claim: Public debt expanded from 67.8% of GDP in 2019 to 80.2% of GDP in mid-2026.
qualification: Ministry of Finance official debt execution reports.

claim: BCT policy interest rate was 7.75% in 2019 vs 8.00% in 2026.
qualification: Banque Centrale de Tunisie Monetary Policy Committee official decisions.

claim: Foreign exchange reserves covered 109 days in 2019 vs 112 days in Summer 2026.
qualification: Banque Centrale de Tunisie daily financial indicators.

claim: Primary energy trade deficit was 49% in 2019 vs 52% in Summer 2026.
qualification: National Energy Observatory (ONME) monthly energy balance.

claim: Moody's rated Tunisia B2 (2019), B3 (Feb 2021), Caa1 (Oct 2021), Caa2 (Jan 2023), affirmed at Caa2 Stable on March 22, 2024 through 2026.
qualification: Moody's official sovereign rating notices.

claim: Fitch rated Tunisia B+ (2019), B- (2021), CCC (2022), CCC- (2023), and upgraded to CCC+ on March 29, 2024 through 2026.
qualification: Fitch Ratings official credit action releases.

claim: Trust in the President was 62% in Wave VII (2022) and declined to 43% in Wave VIII (2024).
qualification: Arab Barometer probability samples (n=2,424 in 2022; n=2,406 in 2024; ±2.5% MoE).

claim: Youth migration intention (ages 18–29) was 42% in 2018/19, 46% in 2022, and 53% in 2024.
qualification: Arab Barometer youth demographic subgroup (ages 18–29).

claim: EU-Tunisia MoU was signed on July 16, 2023 in Tunis; allocated €105M for border management and €150M in direct budgetary aid (disbursed March 2024).
qualification: Official European Commission Press Release IP/23/3887.

claim: IMF staff-level agreement for $1.9B was reached on October 15, 2022, but execution stalled without Executive Board submission.
qualification: IMF Press Release No. 22/353.

claim: ELMED is a 600 MW, 200 km HVDC undersea cable co-financed by €307.6M EU CEF grant and $268.4M World Bank financing.
qualification: World Bank Project P179247 / European Commission CEF.

claim: Historical nominal phosphogypsum discharge into the Gulf of Gabès is ~14,000 tonnes per day (dry-solid basis).
qualification: Source is 2018 ANPE/World Bank PGSE audit. Clearly labeled as Historical Baseline.

claim: Cabinet communiqué of June 29, 2017 pledged the dismantling and relocation of GCT chemical units; zero units have been relocated by Summer 2026.
qualification: Prime Ministry Cabinet Communiqué of June 29, 2017.
